title: The affine-line counit is invertible
statement:
The affine-line counit is invertible on every coefficient complex.
Source: blueprint lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace, proof steps 2--6
(blueprint: lem-amb-affine-trace-line-counit-iso).

Proof: apply open-closed localization to the shifted Tate line on the projective
line, then apply proper direct image. The closed vertex is the shifted Tate line
on the base, because the infinity section is finite and its composite with the
projection is identity. In the normalized projective-line decomposition the map
to this vertex is first projection: the unit restricts to identity, and the Chern
class restricts to zero since O(1) is trivial along the infinity section. The
trace is second projection. Exactness of the cohomology sequence therefore makes
the restricted trace an isomorphism. The composite adjunction identifies this map
with its counit at the tensor unit. For arbitrary K, open tensor comparison and
the proper projection formula identify the counit with K tensor this trace.
The open comparison commutes with counits by the adjunction triangle identity;
proper projection naturality gives the remaining square. Tensoring preserves
isomorphisms. This also covers unbounded K, the empty base, and the zero ring.

Precise quantified statement:
theorem affineTraceLineCounit_isIso (A : Type (u + 1)) [CommRing A] [Finite A] (N : ℕ)
    (hN : 0 < N) (hA : (N : A) = 0) (t : OrdinaryFiniteTwistTransport A N hA)
    (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian S] (hS : IsUnit (N : Γ(S, ⊤)))
    (D : OrdinaryFiniteP1Datum A N hA t S hS) (K : DerivedCategoryModule A S) :
    IsIso ((affineTraceLineAdjunction A N hA t S hS D).counit.app K)

proof.text: Apply the affine-line localization triangle. Write a for its first map, r for restriction, b:B⊕K≅Y for its middle-term coordinates, and t:Y→K for the projective counit. The first component of b r is identity and b t is the second projection.

Let q=in₂ b r. Then b r=pr₁+q pr₂. Precompose b with the triangular automorphism (x,y)↦(x-q y,y), whose inverse is (x,y)↦(x+q y,y). In these new coordinates, b r=pr₁ and b t=pr₂. The section in₁ b forces the connecting arrow w to be zero since r w=0. Map the resulting distinguished triangle to the split triangle K→K⊕B→B. The components are a t, b⁻¹ followed by the biproduct swap, and id_B. All three squares follow from the triangle equations and coordinate identities. Its last two components are isomorphisms, so Mathlib Pretriangulated.isIso₁_of_isIso₂₃ proves a t invertible. Adjunction.comp_counit_app identifies it with the specified affine-line counit.

proof_origin.place: G1 Lean proof: triangular coordinate change, morphism to a split distinguished triangle, and composite-adjunction counit formula. The Kummer restriction computation and cohomology argument are unnecessary.
